lines:
HISTORY RETENTION LANDED. THE LIVE STORE WENT FROM 30.8 GB TO 2.3 GB.

MEASURED OUTCOME (live profile, 2026-10-05)
- file 31,552 MB -> 2,349 MB (29.2 GB reclaimed, 13.4x); WAL 0; free pages 0.
- semantic_events payload 15.0 GB -> 2,015 MB over 597,746 events; 13,326 payloads are tombstones.
- The 30.8 GB was TWO copies of one history. Besides the 15.0 GB payload (context.checkpoint 7,506 MB + model-call span.started 7,507 MB), delivery_outbox held 15,523 MB over 573,690 rows, every one already delivered, mirroring those same payloads. Retention now removes already-delivered delivery records and keeps the newest 512 (cursor monotonicity + acknowledgement grace): 512 rows / 12 MB remain with the maximum cursor preserved.
- 31 Chats the user had deleted lost their events and their attempts/checkpoints/delivery rows; their index tombstones stay, so the sidebar is unchanged. Streams 140 -> 133.
- Retained floor: the two superseded kinds still hold 1,662 MB by design - every Chat keeps its newest snapshot of every context scope plus its newest 20 turns, which is what resumption reads.
- Live verification: the profile opens; all 124 indexed Chats project; every Chat that has a checkpoint (68 of 68) still has at least one intact one; every Chat's model-call window is exactly 20.

DELIVERED
1. Per-scope retention and tombstones (runtime/history_retention.rs): newest per (ownerKey, nodeId, child) scope, newest 20 turns per scope, newest 20 model-call inputs. A release writes a prunedPayload marker (kind, bytes, digestBefore, prunedAt, retainedTurns, reason) and keeps event identity, kind, sequence, timing, usage and hasInput.
2. Automatic write-path bound: an append releases at most 4 payloads it just displaced, from the warm committed view, newest first, over a bounded 4,096-event look-back. A truncated scan can only leave work for the next append - never release a payload still inside the window, never the newest of a scope. The release is applied to the warm view too, so a later append cannot decide it again. A failure there is never reported and can never end a Run.
3. Explicit "Reclaim space" in Settings > Data: measured store size, payload, superseded pool, deleted-Chat bytes, delivery records and kind breakdown, the policy in plain words, what it can release before it starts, a confirmation, and two-phase progress. Never runs at startup.
4. Deleted-Chat purge honouring FOREIGN KEY (chat_id, branch_id) REFERENCES chat_streams: events, attempts, checkpoints and delivery rows before the stream head, in one transaction. The first pass died on this with "FOREIGN KEY constraint failed" on the 19th deleted Chat.
5. Timeline and Run details state a released payload as an omission instead of silently showing less (shared ReleasedPayloadNotice).
6. Fixed a live-profile lockout: the legacy migration re-verifies `chat.local` against each migrated Chat on EVERY open, and payload equality refused the profile with "partially migrated Chat history differs from its legacy source". A released tombstone on either side is now tolerated; the kind must still match, and any other difference is still refused. The regression test was verified to fail on the old predicate.
7. Invariants verified in code before writing: the only readers of a checkpoint snapshot or a model-call input are context_snapshot and select_context, and both already skip released payloads; no verification re-hashes a stored payload (state_hash is only compared against the current projection, the frozen record hashes live configuration, the broker batch identity is write-time only); verify_durable_commit never reaches a delivered delivery record.

EVIDENCE
- cargo test --lib (desktop): 610 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored. cargo test -p aworkit-local-store --all-targets: 76 passed, 0 failed.
- New tests: 4 write-path/scope/idempotence tests in history.rs, the legacy-migration regression, 2 store tests (a purge keeps the cursor and pending rows; deleting a stream removes its FK children), 19 TS tests across the Settings panel and the released-payload rendering.
- TS: tsc --noEmit clean; vitest src/workbench 310 passed; vitest src/chat 282 passed with 3 pre-existing host-environment failures (locale number grouping; two expecting a bash shell).
- qa/milestone-02.sh: formatting and the store tests pass; it still stops at qa/check-boundaries.sh on a PRE-EXISTING violation (aworkit-capability-host depends on aworkit-process-platform, at HEAD since 5abab1f), not from this work. The task-184 gate command (cargo test --lib frozen_record_compat) passes 12/12. The Adashi QA runner could not execute either job in this environment ("Failed to start QA command: program not found" - the jobs' bash shell is unavailable).

CAVEATS
- A release is per stream, so the legacy stream `chat.local` and each Chat migrated from it keep separate windows; that is exactly what the migration tolerance covers.
- A fork or replay from an intermediate turn may no longer find that turn's exact snapshot and must state that rather than invent context; fork or continuation at the head is unaffected.
- The Settings reclaim ceiling adds all delivery-record bytes, so it can overstate (never understate) the release by the undelivered share; the measured row shows delivered versus total.
- One full-suite run showed a load-dependent flake in compaction_integration::successive_actual_compactions_rearm_missing_scopes_and_preserve_partial_survival, which uses an ephemeral committer and passes both in isolation and in subsequent full runs.
- The working tree is not committed.

WHY
A 30.8 GB history store with no retention. Measured 2026-10-05 on the live profile after a WAL checkpoint:
- context.checkpoint 7,694 events = 7,506 MB
- model_call span.started 7,923 events = 7,507 MB
Those two are ~97% of the 15.0 GB payload, and they are the SAME turn's context stored twice (adjacent sequences; up to 2.9 MB each on ~800k-token contexts). Everything else is small: all tool data (9,866 tool_call spans + 9,906 tool.requested) is 31 MB; all internal non-sidebar streams are 14 MB; 482k span.content_delta are 197 MB. 29 of 153 Chats are tombstoned (deleted in the UI) and their events are still stored.

DECIDED POLICY (product owner, 2026-10-05)
Never pruned - nothing here can surprise a user:
- every Chat index entry (created/selected/pinned/deleted): nothing vanishes from the sidebar
- the conversation: user/assistant messages and cards
- tool call records, results, usage, timing: the whole Chat stays visible
- per Chat: the NEWEST context.checkpoint per (nodeId, ownerKey, child) scope AND the newest 20 turns of checkpoints; the newest 20 model-call inputs; anything the head needs to continue
Pruned, visibly - once a turn is superseded:
- superseded context.checkpoint payloads and superseded model_call span.started.input bodies are replaced by a tombstone carrying {pruned: true, digestBefore, bytes, prunedAt, retainedUntil, reason}; the event identity, kind, sequence, timing, usage and hasInput flag stay, so Run details still renders and the timeline can say "request snapshot not retained" instead of silently showing less.
- A fork or replay from an intermediate turn may no longer find that turn's exact snapshot. It must report that explicitly rather than failing or inventing context. Fork/replay from the head is unaffected. This is the accepted tradeoff.
Hard constraints: no silent deletion of content; every Chat must continue from where it ended; the whole Chat stays visible for the main Chat; committed conversation and authority are never rewritten; an unreachable/absent payload must degrade to a notice, never end a Run (aworkit.workflow_worker.failure_policy).

SCOPE
1. Purge of already-tombstoned Chats (29 today). They are already gone from the sidebar, so deleting their events is not silent deletion. Measure first, then remove, and record the purge.
2. Write-path trim (automatic, incremental, invisible): when a checkpoint or model-call input is appended, prune what falls outside the window for that Chat. Must be cheap per append and must never rewrite the newest per scope.
3. Explicit reclaim for the existing backlog: a user-visible action ("Reclaim space") with progress, because rewriting ~15,700 rows of ~1 MB plus VACUUM is heavy. It must never run silently at startup. Report what it will reclaim before doing it.
4. VACUUM (or auto_vacuum=INCREMENTAL enabled once) is what actually shrinks the file; deleting rows alone only frees pages. Needs ~31 GB free.
5. Settings shows the policy and the current store size, so none of this is invisible.
6. The timeline/Run details render a tombstone as a stated omission.

READ FIRST
- aworkit.workflow_worker.failure_policy (normative: no condition ends an Agent node; dispatch degrades).
- aworkit.trusted_core.snapshot_freezer (the unit of configuration stability is one pass; every pass re-resolves; the checkpoint is a prefix/resumption authority, not conversation).
- The debug-capture store already implements the pattern to copy: purge_after_epoch_ms, tombstones, a 'purged' state and a maintenance pass (aworkit-local-store maintenance.rs / common.rs).
- Project memory note handover-comfyui-tool-name-wedge and the task #185/#184 memos for how the store and the frozen records relate.

INVARIANTS AND RISKS TO VERIFY IN CODE BEFORE WRITING
- Which payloads are covered by a stored hash or a checkpoint/state hash: the frozen record's context_hash covers the frozen-context event's context value, not these events, but confirm nothing else hashes a checkpoint or a span input. A pruned payload must not fail any verification.
- Resumption reads: find every reader of context.checkpoint and of a model-call span input, and prove the newest per scope plus the last 20 turns is enough. If any reader walks history backwards, it must tolerate a tombstone.
- Projections: desktop/src/chat/activityProjection.ts, runDetails.ts and the Rust projections must accept a pruned payload without dropping the row.
- Sequence, outbox and index invariants: rows may be updated or deleted, but sequence numbers, chat_streams heads, the delivery outbox and the history index must stay consistent.

ACCEPTANCE
- A fixture Chat with 50 checkpoints across 3 owner scopes and 50 model-call inputs: after the pass, exactly the newest per scope plus the newest 20 turns remain intact; every other payload is a tombstone with digestBefore and bytes; the newest payload is byte-identical to before.
- The conversation, tool records, usage and timing of that Chat are unchanged, and a projection/render test shows the tombstone as a stated omission.
- Continuing that Chat at its head still works (test), and a head fork still works.
- The 29 tombstoned Chats are gone and their bytes reclaimed; the sidebar is unchanged for every non-tombstoned Chat.
- cargo test --lib green; the QA job from task #184 still passes.
- Measured outcome on the live profile recorded in the completion memo: store size before/after, and the resulting payload breakdown.
- Design recorded: a Markdown document 'Canonical history retention: what is kept, what is tombstoned' bound to aworkit.local_store, and this task finished with the numbers.

data.title: Canonical history retention: keep the conversation, the index and the head; tombstone superseded context snapshots and model-call inputs (newest 1 per scope + last 20 turns)
